chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام, who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: Do not bare your teeth openly while you have committed disgraceful deeds, and do not feel secure from the night assault while you have committed evil deeds.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin, the title of Imam Ali عليه السلام
key_terms.الْأَعْمَالَ الْفَاضِحَةَ: disgraceful deeds that expose a person to shame
key_terms.الْبَيَاتَ: a sudden night assault; here, a metaphor for unexpected punishment
key_terms.وَاضِحَةٍ: the visible teeth; an expression for openly smiling or showing cheer

ai.seo_question: Why should a sinner not feel secure after committing evil deeds?
ai.summary: This hadith warns against false ease, shamelessness, and feeling secure despite committing sins. It teaches that evil deeds expose a person to disgrace and to divine punishment, so one should remain vigilant and morally accountable.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbat, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineenasws said: ‘You should not show (your teeth) clearly and you have done the shameful deed, nor should he sleep securely, the one who had committed the sins’.
en.sarwar: 21. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Amir al-Mu’minin, Ali ibn abu Talib (a.s.) has said, ‘Do not show your teeth (smile) if you have committed disgraceful sins. Do not feel safe from misfortunes if you have performed evil deeds.’”
